newsitem.title: USA: Warner-Lambert, Sankyo in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Warner-Lambert, Sankyo in joint venture.

text.p: Warner-Lambert Co said on Tuesday it signed a letter of intent to form a joint venture partnership in the U.S. with Sankyo Co Ltd.

The two will co-promote the diabetes drug troglitazone and Warner-Lambert's cardiovascular agent Accupril. The joint venture is subject to the completion of final agreements, which should be signed later this year, Warner-Lambert said.
The joint venture will assist Warner-Lambert in marketing troglitazone, a diabetes treatment pending review at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a Warner-Lambert spokesman said.
He said the joint-venture would account for "less than half" of troglitizone marketing.
"The preponderance of the marketing of this product will be done by Parke-Davis" alone, the spokesman said, referring to Warner-Lambert's pharmaceutical unit.
Warner-Lambert and Sankyo will share equally in the joint venture's expenses and profits.
Troglitazone was discovered by Sankyo and co-developed in the United States by Parke-Davis and Sankyo.
The joint venture will be named Sankyo/Parke-Davis and will be owned equally by both companies with each naming three members to the governing board.
Joseph Pieroni will be president of the joint venture. Pieroni is currently vice-president of global marketing planning for Parke-Davis.

Warner-Lambert also said it received the rights to market or co-promote with a Sankyo affiliate troglitazone in other markets. These include Mexico, Central America, South America, Australia, New Zealand and the Philippines.
Warner-Lambert said it may also co-promote in the United States Sankyo products that Sankyo intends to market in the U.S. through a co-promotion agreement.
